page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor operating at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX, AVX-512F, and AES instructions. It features 64.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per virtual core. The instance includes no local storage and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps without hardware acceleration or dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark data reflects mid-tier parallel computing capability paired with constrained single-thread throughput. Single-core tests demonstrate lower-bracket results, with a Geekbench single-core score of 925.0 and weak single-threaded compression performance. In contrast, multi-threaded workloads score within the median range, showing a Geekbench multi-core score of 5662.0 and a multi-core stress-ng result of 11751.7. Uncached memory throughput reaches 77.7 GB/sec for reads and 59.92 GB/sec for writes. In application-focused metrics, it achieves 11.29 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 7.81 GB/sec of static web serving throughput.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the ecs.sn2ne.4xlarge is designed for distributed, multi-threaded tasks that do not require high single-thread clock rates or local low-latency NVMe disks. The absence of built-in storage requires relying on attached network block storage, and network throughput is limited to a 3 Gbps baseline. This configuration is technically aligned with balanced web serving, containerized application clusters, build environments, and in-memory caching layers.

The configuration excludes local storage and discrete GPUs, relying on a 3 Gbps baseline network interface. The server is well configured for standard enterprise workloads, background processing pipelines, continuous integration runners, and mid-sized caching tiers requiring dedicated vCPU allocation without high single-core frequency demands.
